name: Haze, UV and gases (CAMS model)
summary: Model estimates of haze, UV and gases (NO2, SO2, CO) for each city. Haze rises on Saharan dust days. Satellites feed the model, but these are model numbers, not satellite pixels.

el.name: Θολούρα, UV και αέρια (μοντέλο CAMS)
el.summary: Εκτιμήσεις μοντέλου για θολούρα, UV και αέρια (NO2, SO2, CO) για κάθε πόλη. Η θολούρα ανεβαίνει όταν έρχεται σκόνη από τη Σαχάρα. Οι δορυφόροι τροφοδοτούν το μοντέλο, αλλά οι τιμές είναι του μοντέλου, όχι εικονοστοιχεία δορυφόρου.

quality.uncertainty: A grid-cell estimate (11 to 45 km wide). It cannot see one busy road, and it can miss the start, the end or the strength of a Saharan dust event.
known_issues: Satellite data (for example MODIS haze) correct the model, but the numbers are model output: not satellite pixels and not a sensor at the school.
Gases are for 10 m above ground averaged over a whole cell: a busy road reads much higher than its cell.
The service does not say which CAMS model (Europe 11 km or global 45 km) answered for each variable.
The current hour comes from the newest model run, started once or twice a day. UV uses forecast clouds.

upstream.name: MODIS instruments on the Terra and Aqua satellites

use_for: Telling a Saharan dust day: haze, dust and PM10 rise together
A model second opinion on haze and UV for a city
Explaining how satellites feed a computer model
not_for: Calling a street's air good or bad
Presenting the numbers as satellite measurements or as a sensor at the school

notes: Saharan dust story: on a dust day the haze here, the dust and PM10 values of the Air quality model layer and the PM10 of the official stations rise together; the UV aerosol index of Sentinel-5P (layer Air from space) is the satellite's own signal.
